_readme: Genjutsu object swap (Higgsfield `hf_mult_replace_object`): put OUR cast or product into the swipe's own shot, keeping its motion. It is the FALLBACK for a swipe ad, behind motion control.

Rewritten 2026-10-27: the old 'never the master alone / send the whole sheet' rule is replaced by the baseline rule (the owner, 2026-10-27), and the finding that a swap replaces and never adds is kept. Maker documentation is thin; the rows that rest on our findings say so.
No brand, product, person or format word appears in this file.
Draft: every entry is status draft until the owner approves it.
label: Genjutsu object swap

vendor_ids.path: higgsfield/genjutsu/object-swap/v1.0 (the one path proven on our door)

sources: [vendor, live] Higgsfield connector model list (models_explore get), read 2026-10-26
[ours] tools/video-production/CLAUDE.md 'A swap is the whole character'

limits.min_shot_seconds: a clean shot of at least about 2 s with no cut inside (ours); the model's minimum is 4 s, a shorter shot is played forward-back-forward to reach it and trimmed (ours, 18 Oct)
limits.price_per_second_usd: from 0.159 (list 0.318) at Genjutsu; about 8.3 credits a second measured at 1080p (ours)
limits.maker_documentation: Higgsfield publishes no step-by-step page for Object Swap; its blog describes the mode and a third-party guide tested it. Limits above the vendor's list are OURS, measured.

house.per_shot: one swap per shot, never one pass over a clip with cuts
house.person: a cast member's BASELINE (headshot, look, details, expressions), never the master (the owner, 2026-10-27; replaces the earlier 'send the whole sheet' line)

inputs.name: video_references
inputs.what: The swipe's own shot to take the motion and the scene from.
inputs.allowed: one video, a clean single shot, model minimum 4 s
inputs.we_send: one shot cut on the frame map's boundaries

inputs.name: image_references
inputs.what: What goes in: the cast member's BASELINE pictures (headshot, look, details, expressions), or the product photo.
inputs.we_send: the baseline pictures that fit the shot (headshot and look at least); never the master alone and never the master as the person

inputs.name: prompt
inputs.what: The standard swap words: who is replaced by whom, the before or after state, every accessory to remove.
inputs.allowed: text; the maker says presets can do the job with no prompt

inputs.name: preset
inputs.what: A ready swap recipe (person, outfit, product).
inputs.we_send: not used: the standard prompt is ours

inputs.name: target element
inputs.allowed: named in the prompt: one subject, outfit or product

inputs.name: lite variant
inputs.what: Genjutsu Lite, a Kling 4.0 based swap.
inputs.we_send: not used (only the v1.0 path is proven on our door)

inputs.name: audio
inputs.allowed: none: the swap keeps the original mouth and sound
inputs.we_send: not available: a line of ours is laid under at the edit

inputs.name: duration
inputs.allowed: follows the source shot; model minimum 4 s
inputs.we_send: the swipe shot's length, looped forward-back-forward when under 4 s

structure.rule: A swap replaces something that is already in the shot and never adds. Whatever must be on a counter, in a hand or on a wall has to be in the SOURCE shot already, or come from a scene still made first; the swap will not put it there.
structure.ours: a product on a counter comes from the scene still (motion control), not the swap
structure.source: [ours] tools/video-production/SHOT-ROUTES.md ; https://app.therundown.ai/guides/swap-the-product-and-keep-the-performance-with-higgsfield (the swapped prop did not land and the original stayed)

structure.rule: The cast member goes in from the BASELINE pictures, never the master. A swap given the master alone is a face swap; the baseline gives the face, the look, the details and the expressions the shot needs.
Split at the cuts and swap one shot at a time; a whole-clip pass missed people in 4 of 16 shots and put the wrong subject on the wrong person.
structure.ours: per-shot swaps on the frame map's boundaries

structure.rule: State the before and the after state from the brief; everything else, body included, stays identical.
Name every accessory of the original that must go, not only a colour; a headwrap's tails survived when only its colour was removed.
A recast subject is built inside the shot's own light and look, not laid in from a studio sheet.
structure.ours: references show her in a real setting

structure.rule: Every swap is checked against the baseline before it is kept; when the swap kept the original person's face, send the same shot to motion control instead (9 of 9 kept it).
A shot under the 4 s minimum is played forward-back-forward and trimmed; trim the loop seam off.
Before a batch, find a clip and object pair that works reliably: try a different prop in the same source clip, hold the action fixed and compare at the same moment.

avoid.text: Expecting our line from a swap: it keeps the original mouth, so it carries no line of ours.
Expecting it to add things: it replaces, never adds; the product goes only where the swipe already has something in hand.
One swap pass over a clip with several cuts.
Sending the master as the person: it is a face swap, and the baseline is the rule.
A shot shorter than the model's minimum without playing it forward-back-forward.
Removing an accessory by naming only its colour.
A studio-backdrop sheet as the only reference: it reads pasted on.
Keeping a swap without checking the face: 9 of 9 kept the original person.
